name: Antidisestablishmentarianism
summary: Opposition to removing the Church of England's established status, meaning its legal tie to the Crown, Parliament and state ceremony. Defenders argue that establishment gives every English person access to the church's rites, tempers religious and nationalist extremism, and keeps religion tied to the common life of the nation.
scope: The English (and historically Irish and Welsh) defence of the Church of England's establishment from the Victorian disestablishment campaigns to modern defenders such as Phillip Blond and Giles Coren, with Richard Hooker as the classic theorist. It is a single-issue stance, so most answers outside church and state are low-confidence inferences.

farm-price-support.rationale: A single-issue position on church establishment; supporters span the parties and no source states a view.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: A single-issue position on church establishment; no source states a view on nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Defenders emphasise tradition and the nation's common life over class-based politics; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: The Church of England's establishment is tied to shared moral standards and its public role; a ban fits mainstream Anglican opinion, though not a stated tenet.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Mainstream Anglican and conservative opinion accepts equal property rights today; inferred, not stated in the sources.

one-language-many-names.rationale: No stated view; a single-issue position on church establishment.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No stated view; a single-issue position on church establishment.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Defenders favour an established church with a public role in national law through bishops in the Lords, but chiefs are a different tradition; inferred from that principle.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: No stated view; supporters span the parties.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No stated view; supporters span the parties.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Defenders tie religion to the common life of the nation, which suggests support for national cohesion measures; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The stance is about the established church and says nothing on union membership; inferred as neutral.

voter-id.rationale: Not a church-state issue; adherents are split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Establishment gives the Church of England a legal tie to the Crown and Parliament that other churches and faiths lack, which defenders want kept.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Defenders are not committed to either view of democracy; inferred as neutral.

premarital-sex.rationale: The established church teaches marriage as the setting for sex, and its defenders are mostly traditional on this; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Defenders stress the common life of a free nation, so shutdowns are inferred to be unwelcome.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is outside the stance; adherents are split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Modern defenders sit within the Church of England, which ordains women and supports equal political rights; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Defenders argue establishment tempers extremism and that the church serves the whole nation, so they reject the claim; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Defenders are mostly mainstream English conservatives or liberals, who accept the social-construct view; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed by the stance; adherents are split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: A single-issue church-state stance with no view on original acquisition of property; defenders range across the conservative spectrum.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The position does not address international justice and its defenders are split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Church of England is a broad church that includes literalists and liberals, and defenders of establishment argue from national tradition rather than a doctrine of scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only that defenders of establishment hold varied views on group self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, Anglican tradition of its defenders, which is hostile to state socialism; the sources do not discuss it.

indirect-election.rationale: Establishment is about church and Crown, not electoral method; defenders hold no common view.

national-church-status.rationale: This is the defining claim: the Church of England's legal ties to Crown and Parliament (Supreme Governor, bishops in the Lords) set it above other religious bodies, and defenders argue this should continue.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The stance is about church establishment; historically its defenders opposed disestablishment in Wales and Ireland, but nothing in it speaks to ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by the position and not a shared view among defenders.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by the position and not a shared view among defenders.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; the Anglican tradition Hooker defends does not demand limited needs or self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the position; defenders hold no common view.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by the position; defenders are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Defenders say establishment ties religion to the common life of the nation, so a bond with the national land fits loosely; inferred from that rationale.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Hooker's tradition of law and the English constitutional heritage conflict with killing without trial; inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment lies outside the church-state question; no position.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The doctrine concerns the Church of England within England, not kin abroad; inferred as indifferent.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Defenders of establishment tend to be conservative and favour existing property rights; inferred, and the doctrine takes no formal position.

self-ownership.rationale: The doctrine takes no position on self-ownership; inferred as indifferent.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is outside the doctrine; no position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design is outside the doctrine; no position.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Defenders value established institutions, including Parliament and parties, over direct rule by a leader; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The doctrine takes no position on business privileges; inferred as indifferent, although an established church is itself a legal privilege.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Establishment is a legal privilege for one denomination, the Church of England, so antidisestablishmentarians accept that the church has a public role in politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Defenders value tradition and continuity in national life but accept modern society; inferred as a conservative combination.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Adherents are split: the Church of England now accepts civil divorce, but the doctrine takes no position; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource control is outside the doctrine; no position.

distribution-by-process.rationale: A single-issue stance about church establishment; no source states a view on this.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: No source states a view on financial taxation.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Defenders say establishment tempers extremism and serves all English people, which suggests no strong view that racism is gone; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Hooker's account of law ties it to reason and natural law, so an unjust law lacks full authority; inferred from the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The stance has no position on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: The stance has no position on the world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: A conservative defence of tradition makes a labour theory of value unlikely; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Defenders tie religion to the common life of the nation, which fits patriotism; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: The stance has no position on left priorities.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Defenders of the established order are unlikely to back communist-party rule; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A country may properly have an official state church with a formal role in its constitution and national ceremonies.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the core claim of the defence of establishment, stated by the Church and by Blond and Coren.

notes: Advocates are split on other issues (for example same-sex marriage, where the Church of England itself is divided); those are scored 0. Some defenders, such as Hooker, rest the case on theology, others on pragmatic national benefits.
